summary: Trout Brook Mountain tower, Piscataquis County, Maine, listed gone; only the FFLA listing and a hiking guide were readable, so there is no build or fate history.

visit.trail_note: 3.5-mile loop from Trout Brook Farm Campground; the guide says both ascents are steep and lists pets as not allowed

evidence.supports: Trout Brook Mountain tower in Piscataquis County at 46.15008 -68.84415, listed as gone
evidence.quote: Trout Brook Mountain Piscataquis 46.15008 -68.84415 Tower Gone

evidence.supports: Maine by Foot files the mountain under Baxter State Park
Loop begins along the Five Ponds Trail from Trout Brook Farm Campground
evidence.quote: From Trout Brook Farm Campground, the trail begins along the Five Ponds Trail

evidence.supports: Summit given as 1,781 feet, with 1,092 feet of elevation gain
evidence.quote: For me, this was a deceptively difficult mountain (1,781 feet, elevation gain 1,092 feet)
Both ascents, from either side of the loop, are steep.

evidence.supports: Views from the summit are good
evidence.quote: The views from the summit are good

evidence.supports: Counterclockwise recommended; ridge views soon after the summit
evidence.quote: I recommend doing the loop counterclockwise, so you reach the summit first and the ridge with marvelous views soon after.

notes_for_editor: At about 126 words, just over the 120-word floor, because the readable sources support little more: the FFLA listing and a hiking guide that does not mention a tower. A Facebook post from the FFLA Maine chapter came up in search (not readable by fetch_text or WebFetch, so not cited) saying a lookout on Trout Brook Mountain burned in 1915 and that a tower on South Pogy Mountain was built in 1916 to replace it. Verify that before adding it. Do not use the Wikipedia article titled Trout Brook Mountain: it describes a Catskill peak in New York, a different mountain. The hiking guide's 1,781-foot figure has not been checked against a survey.
